name: backups
title: Backups
summary: Backups of the whole system (database, uploaded files, settings and keys) from the Admin Center: the list of backups on the server, a backup now, downloads, uploads and restores with two-person approval. The server's root backup service (deploy/linux ops.sh) does the work; this module asks it through request files and reports what it did.
owns: The list of backups on the server (database, uploaded files, settings and keys) and the nightly schedule
Requests to the server's backup service: back up now, restore, apply the schedule
Backup downloads (database and uploaded files; never the settings and keys file)
Restores: re-authenticated request, typed confirmation, a second staff member's approval (re-authenticated too), a safety backup first
notOwns: Making and restoring backups: the root service on the server (deploy/linux/ops.sh, backup.sh, restore.sh)
Copying backups off the server: staff download them, or copy /var/backups/marketly to a USB disk (deploy/linux/README.md)

id.desc: The backup's time stamp, e.g. 2026-10-15_0230 (server time); an uploaded backup ends in -uploaded

kind.desc: safety: taken automatically just before a restore

files.desc: The uploaded files (media); missing in a database-only backup

hasSettingsAndKeys.desc: The settings and keys file is on the server. It is never downloadable from the web: copy it by USB

state.desc: A restore waits for the second approval; the server's backup service then runs it (queued → running → done or failed)

backupId.desc: backup: the backup made; restore: the backup restored

safetyBackupId.desc: restore: the backup taken just before it

message.desc: What the backup service reported (the error when it failed)

time.desc: HH:MM in the market time zone (setting backups.time)

keepDays.desc: Backups older than this are deleted (setting backups.keepDays)

applied.desc: The server's backup service has this schedule (a change is applied within a minute)

available.desc: False where the server has no backup service (development machines): nothing can be backed up or restored here

running.desc: The backup or restore the service is working on (one at a time)

pendingRestore.desc: A restore waiting for its second approval

warnings.desc: e.g. no backup in the last 26 hours; backups are on the same disk as the data

tables.name: operations
tables.desc: Backups, restores and schedule changes asked of the server's backup service. The service's status file is the truth while it runs; after a restore (which replaces this collection) the module rebuilds its rows from the status files.

tables.name: uploads
tables.desc: Backups uploaded through the Admin Center (the files are in BACKUP_UPLOAD_DIR/<id>/)

stateMachines.name: Backup operation
stateMachines.notes: A restore starts in waiting_approval; a backup and a schedule change start queued. start, finish and fail come from the backup service's status file.

endpoints.summary: Backups on the server, the schedule and what the backup service is doing

endpoints.desc: Asks the server's backup service for a backup (database, uploaded files, settings and keys). One operation runs at a time: OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS while another backup or a restore is queued or running.

endpoints.summary: Download a backup (database and uploaded files)
endpoints.desc: Signed links valid for 15 minutes. The settings and keys file is never offered: it holds APP_SECRET; copy it by USB on the server. Needs the password again (reauthToken, purpose backup-download).
Then send the database file (<date>.archive.gz) and, optionally, the uploaded-files file (<date>.media.tar.gz) to the upload's two PUT endpoints.

endpoints.summary: Send the database file of an uploaded backup
endpoints.desc: The raw bytes of <date>.archive.gz (a gzip file), streamed to the server's disk; up to backups.maxUploadGb.

endpoints.summary: Send the uploaded-files file of an uploaded backup
endpoints.desc: The raw bytes of <date>.media.tar.gz (a gzip file); up to backups.maxUploadGb.

Replaces the whole database and the uploaded files with the backup; everything done since is lost. Needs the password again (reauthToken, purpose backup-restore), confirm = RESTORE and a reason. Always needs a second staff member's approval (access action backups.restore, who confirms with their password too). After the approval the backup service takes a safety backup, stops the server, restores, and starts it again (a few minutes).
endpoints.approval: Always a second staff member (Platform Administrator or another Business Owner), who confirms with their password

endpoints.summary: Withdraw a restore that is still waiting for approval
One backup, restore or schedule change

publishes.name: backups.operation.finished
publishes.when: The backup service finished a backup or restore (done or failed)

consumes.name: access.approval.decided
consumes.does: A restore's approval: approved → the request goes to the backup service; rejected or returned → rejected

consumes.name: settings.setting.changed
consumes.does: backups.time or backups.keepDays changed → asks the backup service to apply the schedule

permissions.desc: See the backups, the schedule and what the backup service is doing. Seeded to the Business Owner and the Platform Administrator
Back up now. Seeded to the Business Owner and the Platform Administrator
Download backups (the whole database and the uploaded files: all customer, seller and staff data). Seeded to the Business Owner only
Upload backups and ask for a restore (always approved by a second person). Seeded to the Business Owner only

approvalActions.desc: Restore a backup over the whole system
approvalActions.approvers: Platform Administrator or a Business Owner other than the requester, who confirms with their password

jobs.name: backups.watch-operations
jobs.does: Reads the backup service's status files: moves operations to running, done or failed, rebuilds rows a restore replaced, and asks for the schedule again when the service hasn't applied it

settings.desc: When the nightly backup runs (market time)
Backups older than this are deleted from the server
Largest backup file that can be uploaded

BACKUPS_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: This server has no backup service (a development machine, or BACKUP_OPS_DIR is not set)

OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS.meaning: Another backup or restore is waiting or running; details.operationId

NOT_A_BACKUP.meaning: The uploaded file is not a gzip file made by the backup service

UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE.meaning: The file is larger than backups.maxUploadGb; details.maxBytes

notes: The work is done by the server's root backup service (deploy/linux/ops.sh, run by marketly-ops.path whenever a request file appears). The web process never runs mongodump, never stops the server and can't read the settings and keys file (root only, mode 600): it writes a request JSON to BACKUP_OPS_DIR/requests and reads BACKUP_OPS_DIR/status/<id>.json. ops.sh treats every request as untrusted: ids, times and numbers are checked before use.

Backups are listed from BACKUP_DIR (/var/backups/marketly, group-readable by the service user): <id>.archive.gz (database), <id>.media.tar.gz (uploaded files), <id>.config.tar.gz (settings and keys, root only) and <id>.manifest.json (kind, note, who asked, sizes).
Downloads are signed /files links of the bucket backups, served by this module from BACKUP_DIR; only .archive.gz and .media.tar.gz names can be signed.

A restore: the requester re-authenticates (backup-restore) and types RESTORE; access.requestApproval (backups.restore, secondReviewer always, stepUp always) routes it to a Platform Administrator or another Business Owner, whose approval needs their password. On access.approval.decided (approved) the module writes the restore request; ops.sh checks the files, takes a safety backup, stops the server, restores the database (mongorestore --drop) and the uploaded files, runs migrate and starts the server.

A restore replaces this module's own collections with the backup's. On boot and every minute the module reads the status files and rebuilds any operation they name that the database no longer has, so the restore and its safety backup stay on the list.
Without BACKUP_OPS_DIR (development machines) the screen says backups are made by the production server, and every action answers BACKUPS_UNAVAILABLE.
